title: Storm-3068 Uses Azure DevOps Pipelines to Harvest Kubeconfig Credentials and Reach Kubernetes
content_md: The attacker abused legitimate identity services, development tools, and trusted pipelines rather than relying on malware or software vulnerabilities. Microsoft’s Detection and Response Team, known as DART , investigated the incident. Its findings show how access to a development platform can expose cloud credentials and deployment infrastructure when permissions connect these systems too closely. The attack began with a successful self-service password reset. Storm-3068 then registered its own authentication methods to maintain control of the account. Microsoft’s attack timeline also recorded the removal of legitimate multifactor authentication methods and registration of an attacker-controlled device in Intune. Storm-3068 Steals Kubernetes Credentials Using valid account credentials, Storm-3068 explored Azure DevOps repositories, projects, pipelines, and deployment environments. Automated scripts and administrative tools helped the attacker identify connected resources and trusted deployment paths. These details provided a map for moving beyond the initial account. The attacker created a malicious pipeline using permissions available to the compromised identity. That pipeline was authorized to access more than 50 resources, giving the actor a broad collection opportunity within the development environment.
